about: Lesson 11 (T11, 11-solver). Prairie Town is fictional; its plants, costs and the unserved-energy penalty are illustrative. The day is lesson 0's (3 September 2025, SPP shapes from EIA-930 in town_year.json). 'rule', 'signError', 'threshold' and 'precomputed' are written by node _tests/learn/test_11-solver.js --write from the lesson-0 model (grid-operator.js) and this lesson's model with the vendored HiGHS; the page solves live and uses 'precomputed' only if the solver cannot load. The test fails if any of them drifts.
penaltyNote: Cost per MWh of unserved demand: a large illustrative number so that the solver keeps the lights on whenever it can.

facts.what: HiGHS, the solver on this page, is open source under the MIT licence; it solves linear programs by simplex, interior point or first-order methods, and mixed-integer programs by branch-and-cut.
How often the western Energy Imbalance Market dispatched generating units, as EIA reported in July 2017: real operators re-solve dispatch problems like this one every few minutes.
